Puzzle 9 · 10 of 11

When the connection breaks

Puzzle 0 said TCP resends lost packets. Yet requests still fail after a while, and sometimes you can't tell whether the server did the work. Here's where TCP's promise ends, and the question the app then can't answer.

  • Puzzle 0: What actually travels

    Data crosses the internet in packets. IP addresses each packet and routes it, but can lose, delay or reorder it. TCP turns those packets into a reliable, ordered stream: it numbers them, waits for acknowledgements and resends what's lost, and needs a connection set up first. TLS encrypts that stream, and HTTP is the language of requests and responses on top.

The problem

The user taps Pay in a lift. After ten seconds, OkHttp throws a SocketTimeoutException. TCP was supposed to resend whatever got lost. So why did it fail, and, the question that matters: was the payment made or not?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

TCP resends lost packets, but only while the connection exists and both ends can still reach each other. On a phone, that ends all the time: a lift, a tunnel, a switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data. Then the packets have nowhere to go, and TCP can't help.

So the app can't wait forever. OkHttp gives up after a timeout, and there are two kinds you'll meet:

  • Connect timeout: no connection could be made at all. The request never left: safe to try again.
  • Read timeout: the connection was made and the request was sent, but no answer arrived in time.

The read timeout is the dangerous one. It has two possible stories, and from the phone they look identical:

  1. The request was lost on the way: the server never saw it.
  2. The server did the work, and the answer was lost on the way back.

That's the question a timeout can't answer: did it happen? For reading data, it doesn't matter: ask again. For a payment or an order, retrying could do it twice. Puzzle 10 is the fix.

The analogy

Posting a cheque and hearing nothing back. Maybe the post lost your letter; maybe the bank cashed it and the receipt got lost. From your sofa, you can't tell which.

Check yourself

A read timeout fires on POST /orders. What do you know?

Not quite. The server may have answered; only the answer went missing.

Right. A read timeout can't say if it happened.

Not quite. TCP resends packets inside one request; it doesn't send the request twice.

A connect timeout fires. Is it safe to retry a payment request?

Not quite. No connection means nothing was sent; there's nothing to check.

Not quite. With no connection, the request couldn't reach the server.

Right. No connection, nothing sent.

What's the difference between a connect timeout and a read timeout?

Not quite. That's the two swapped. Re-read that part ↑

Right. Never left vs no answer back.

Sources

  • High Performance Browser Networking: Building blocks of TCP (TCP's reliability: "retransmission of lost data, in-order delivery" over a connection)

What you now know

TCP is reliable only while the connection lasts; on a phone, connections break in lifts, tunnels and handovers between Wi-Fi and mobile data. OkHttp gives up after timeouts: connect (no connection made) and read (no answer arrived). A read timeout can't tell you whether the server did the work: the request may have arrived and the answer been lost. Puzzle 10 makes that safe to retry.
